name: Remove external exposure
label: Remove external exposure
credit_rule: Assume verified removal of public ingress across the selected scope. An established inbound vulnerable service supports ordinary marginal benefit without proof of actual customer public exposure or internet-origin attackers; internal and permitted peers remain residual. Explicitly internal-only, adjacent-only or outbound-client routes receive no public-ingress benefit. AV:N alone is insufficient.
direction_rule: Removes public ingress. Does nothing when the attacker is a server the victim connects out to.

name: Segmentation and restrictive ACLs
label: Segmentation and restrictive ACLs
credit_rule: Assume restrictive ACLs are verified across the relevant selected network paths. Ordinary credit requires a source-established entry or delivery mechanism whose attacker traffic or peer eligibility is restricted; permitted or compromised peers may remain residual. Marginal benefit does not require total elimination. Distinct internal lateral restriction is not erased by partial overlap with public-ingress removal; the existing engine still applies its frozen combined cap.

name: Disable vulnerable service or feature
label: Disable vulnerable service or feature
credit_rule: Assess an already disabled service or feature across the selected scope. Ordinary benefit requires a named source-established required service operation or feature, not an optionality claim or vendor recommendation. A bare driver/component name or unspecified local interface alone is insufficient. The verification_requirements list governs strong exact-path claims, not ordinary benefit. Strong exact-path credit requires CVE-specific vendor disablement evidence and covered exploit paths unavailable. A vendor statement that disabled systems are not exploitable is valid; operational undesirability does not erase its benefit. Preserve consumer-specific scope and patch floors.

name: Apply vendor workaround
label: Apply vendor workaround
credit_rule: Assume the selected workaround is verified across its relevant scope. Credit requires a source-grounded CVE-specific mechanism; unknown prerequisites receive zero. Strong exact-path credit requires the exact cited vendor workaround and unavailable covered exploit paths, not merely a security-update or Known Issue link. Preserve consumer/product scope and patch floors.

name: Exploit-specific IPS or NGFW rule
label: Exploit-specific IPS or NGFW rule
credit_rule: Credit requires a CVE-specific or exploit-specific signature in prevention mode with recent validation.

name: WAF virtual patch
label: WAF virtual patch
credit_rule: Credit requires coverage of the vulnerable route and a tested blocking rule.
direction_rule: Inspects inbound requests to a protected service. Not in the path of an outbound client request.

name: Protocol or feature hardening
label: Protocol or feature hardening
credit_rule: Credit requires a setting that directly removes an exploit prerequisite.

name: Strong authentication and access restriction
label: Strong authentication and access restriction
credit_rule: Credit only when authentication gates the vulnerable path and bypass routes are excluded.

name: Least privilege and privileged access management
label: Least privilege and privileged access management
credit_rule: Primarily reduces consequence unless the exploit requires privileges that have been removed.

name: Application control or WDAC
label: Application control or WDAC
credit_rule: Credit only when the inferred exploit chain depends on starting an untrusted executable or script.

name: Attack surface reduction rules
label: Attack surface reduction rules
credit_rule: Credit requires a rule that maps to the inferred exploit technique and is enforced.

name: Email and web content filtering
label: Email and web content filtering
credit_rule: Assume verified restriction of the established mail or browser content-delivery path, not exploit recognition. Ordinary marginal benefit does not require a published malicious URL or signature or elimination of every permitted/compromised sender or destination. Preserve those residuals, require a supported user-content path, and never claim an exact block from generic filtering presence.

name: Office Protected View and macro hardening
label: Office Protected View and macro hardening
credit_rule: Credit applies only to Office exploit paths addressed by the configured policy.

name: EDR exploit-specific prevention
label: EDR exploit-specific prevention
credit_rule: Credit requires a tested prevention capability for the specific exploit behavior, not generic EDR presence.

name: EDR detection and response coverage
label: EDR detection and response coverage
credit_rule: No likelihood credit by default. This improves detection and response confidence.

name: Immutable and tested backups
label: Immutable and tested backups
credit_rule: No likelihood credit. This may reduce availability consequences but not confidentiality or identity compromise.

name: Strong isolation or offline enclave
label: Strong isolation or offline enclave
credit_rule: Assume verified isolation of relevant entry/delivery and administration paths across the selected scope. Ordinary credit requires a source-established network mechanism and supported marginal removal of opportunity; permitted peers inside the isolation boundary may remain residual. Later local processing does not erase explicitly established network delivery. Local/physical entry alone receives no network credit. Never an exact vendor path block.
exact_path_note: Isolation overlap metadata does not make this control exact-path eligible.
